exposure: Selective uterine fundal pressure maneuver (UFPM) during the second stage of the first twin delivery
cohort: The study included 64 cases of trial of vaginal delivery of twins at a single institute between 2002 and 2012.
finding: The study found that selective UFPM during the first twin delivery was associated with increased postpartum hemorrhage, but no significant differences in neonatal outcomes between those who received the maneuver and those who did not.
mod_finding: The findings suggest that selective uterine fundal pressure maneuver performed during the second stage of vaginal delivery for the first twin is not unsafe for the mother and babies, despite an increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
